text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000086 bills 99215 far above its complexity-adjusted expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but the returned charts largely support the billed levels, so the pattern is unresolved.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern points toward upcoding: the 99215 excess is concentrated on patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions, where sampled diagnoses are routine (URI, rash, back pain, UTI, follow-up Z09, as in C0045970, C0046056 and C0046072), and the overall mix leans heavily toward 99214. Against that, the 99215 charts that came back show an unsupported rate close to the comparison providers, including high-MDM support on a low-complexity visit such as C0046114. That support rests on a small documented sample covering under a tenth of claims. The note signals leave room for documentation that does not match the visit: problem-related flags are common, time entries repeat in some notes, and a few notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim, which is weak evidence of inflated notes rather than proof. A reviewer should first pull the flagged notes C0045970, C0045974 and C0045994 and check whether the documented problems and data review fit simple acute complaints, then request more charts for low-complexity 99215 visits to see whether the support holds."}
